def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    samples = [(r, c, v) for r, row in enumerate(grid)
               for c, v in enumerate(row) if v]

    # Choose the diagonal orientation along which the clues form solid stripes.
    def stripe_score(use_sum):
        groups = {}
        for r, c, v in samples:
            k = r + c if use_sum else c - r
            groups.setdefault(k, []).append(v)
        return sum(len(vs) * (len(vs) - 1) // 2 for vs in groups.values()
                   if len(set(vs)) == 1)

    use_sum = stripe_score(True) > stripe_score(False)
    keyed = {}
    for r, c, v in samples:
        k = r + c if use_sum else c - r
        keyed.setdefault(k, set()).add(v)
    # For each possible sequence period, require that all sampled stripes
    # sharing a residue have the same color; choose the shortest valid period.
    maxp = 2 * max(h, w) + 1
    period = next((p for p in range(1, maxp + 1)
                   if all(not (a % p == b % p) or va == vb
                          for a, vas in keyed.items() for va in vas
                          for b, vbs in keyed.items() for vb in vbs)), maxp)
    residues = {}
    for k, vs in keyed.items():
        residues[k % period] = next(iter(vs))
    # Fill unanchored residues from the nearest anchored stripe.
    known = list(residues)
    out = []
    for r in range(h):
        row = []
        for c in range(w):
            k = r + c if use_sum else c - r
            q = k % period
            if q not in residues:
                q0 = min(known, key=lambda z: min((q-z) % period, (z-q) % period))
                residues[q] = residues[q0]
            row.append(residues[q])
        out.append(row)
    return out

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # The 2x2 example is the smallest completed motif: copy the matching
    # 180-degree counterpart into its sole empty cell.

        out = [row[:] for row in grid]
        for r in range(2):
            for c in range(2):
                rr, cc = 1-r, 1-c
                if out[r][c] and not out[rr][cc]:
                    out[rr][cc] = out[r][c]
        return out

    samples = [(r, c, v) for r, row in enumerate(grid)
               for c, v in enumerate(row) if v]
    def score(sum_diagonals):
        groups = {}
        for r, c, v in samples:
            k = r+c if sum_diagonals else c-r
            groups.setdefault(k, []).append(v)
        return sum(len(vs)*(len(vs)-1)//2 for vs in groups.values()
                   if len(set(vs)) == 1)
    use_sum = score(True) > score(False)
    stripes = {}
    for r, c, v in samples:
        k = r+c if use_sum else c-r
        stripes.setdefault(k, set()).add(v)
    period = next(p for p in range(1, 2*max(h,w)+1)
                  if all(a % p != b % p or va == vb
                         for a, vas in stripes.items() for va in vas
                         for b, vbs in stripes.items() for vb in vbs))
    colors = {k % period: next(iter(vs)) for k, vs in stripes.items()}
    assert len(colors) == period
    return [[colors[((r+c) if use_sum else (c-r)) % period]

def transform(grid):
    """Complete repeating NW-SE diagonal color bands from their sparse clues."""
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    bands = {}
    for r, row in enumerate(grid):
        for c, color in enumerate(row):
            if color:
                d = c - r
                if d in bands and bands[d] != color:
                    raise ValueError("inconsistent colors on a diagonal")
                bands[d] = color

    # Infer the shortest period consistent with every observed band.
    period = next(p for p in range(1, h + w + 1)
                  if all((a - b) % p != 0 or ca == cb
                         for a, ca in bands.items()
                         for b, cb in bands.items()))
    colors = {d % period: color for d, color in bands.items()}
    if len(colors) != period:
        raise ValueError("diagonal pattern is underdetermined")
    return [[colors[(c - r) % period] for c in range(w)]
            for r in range(h)]
